qs.q: Which of the following would perform the required mathematical and logic operations of a central processing unit (CPU)?
qs.x: The arithmetic-logic unit (ALU) does all arithmetic and logical operations.

qs.q: Which one executes the program's instructions?
qs.x: The control unit carries out (executes) instructions and coordinates hardware.

qs.q: Which one of the following properties of a central processing unit (CPU) is measured in gigahertz (GHz)?
qs.x: CPU speed is measured in gigahertz (GHz).

qs.q: What does CPU speed refer to?
o: The number of machine cycles a CPU performs per second
The amount of time taken by a CPU to send data to main memory
The amount of time taken by the CPU to write to a secondary storage device
The number of reads a CPU performs per minute
qs.x: CPU speed = the number of machine cycles performed per second.

qs.q: What hardware component is used for temporary storage of data and applications for processing?
qs.x: RAM holds the data and instructions the CPU is working on right now.

qs.q: Which one of the following categories does RAM belong to?
qs.x: RAM is part of main (primary) memory, not secondary storage.

qs.q: Which of the following memory chips are used to store fixed (permanent) start-up instructions?
qs.x: ROM is non-volatile and holds permanent start-up (manufacturer's) instructions.

qs.q: Which of the following are two examples of a secondary storage?
o: USB flash Drive and floppy Disk
USB flash Drive and RAM chip
qs.x: Secondary storage is permanent storage: flash drives, floppy disks, hard disks, CDs.

qs.q: The type of optical disk designed to enable recording, rewriting and playback of high-definition (HD) video, as well as storing large amounts of data is called what?
qs.x: Blu-ray is the optical disc designed for high-definition video and large data.

qs.q: Which devices are small, non-volatile secondary storage media with no moving parts and are portable and often used with digital cameras, handheld computers, laptops, and the like
qs.x: Flash memory: small, non-volatile, no moving parts, used in cameras and phones.

qs.q: Which of the following is used to save to and read data from a secondary storage medium?
qs.x: A drive is the device that reads from and writes to a storage medium.

qs.q: How many bytes make up a kilobyte?
qs.x: 1 kilobyte = 1,024 bytes (2 to the power 10).

qs.q: In computing terms, what does each zero and one signal represent?
qs.x: A single 0 or 1 is a bit; 8 bits make a byte.

qs.q: In computing terms what is a group of 8 bits called?
qs.x: 8 bits = 1 byte.

qs.q: In computing terms what is a byte?
o: Representation of a single character in a computer
A combination of characters and symbols in a computer
Length of a word in a computer
qs.x: A byte represents one character in a computer.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a peripheral device?
qs.x: Peripherals are external devices; primary memory is inside the system unit.

qs.q: What does sending of a document over a phone line by converting a computer's digital signals to analog signals use?
qs.x: A modem converts digital signals to analogue so they travel over a phone line.

qs.q: Which device converts digital computer signals into analog signals so that they can be sent over a telephone line?
qs.x: Same point: modem = modulator/demodulator, digital to analogue and back.

qs.q: Which of the following are communication devices?
o: Fiber optic cable, Ethernet cable, Wi-Fi
qs.x: Modem, router and server are communications devices; a printer is output.

qs.q: What is a system of interconnected computers, telephones or communications devices that can communicate and share resources called?
qs.x: A network is interconnected computers and devices that communicate and share resources.

qs.q: What is a Server?
o: A computer that provide services and resources to other computers
Acomputer that requests services and resources from other computers
A special computer designed for technical or scientific applications
qs.x: A server holds data and programs and supplies services to client computers.

qs.q: In network terms the ability of a computer to share and control access to its services by other computers makes it which of the following?
qs.x: Sharing and controlling access to its services makes a computer the server.

qs.q: In a client-server network, what is a central computer that supplies data or services requested of it called?
qs.x: In a client-server network the central computer supplying services is the server.

qs.q: Which type of a server acts like a disk drive, storing programs and data files shared by users on a LAN?
qs.x: A file server stores the programs and data files shared by users on a LAN.

qs.q: What category of computers are expensive, powerful and are generally used for complex scientific, mathematical and engineering calculations?
qs.x: The official answer is Supercomputers. Careful: Lecture 1 describes workstations in almost the same words (scientific, mathematical, engineering, CAD), so read the options closely.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
o: Mainframe computers can handle a large number of transactions and users
The contents of ROM are deleted when the computer is switched off
qs.x: Mainframes support hundreds of users and huge numbers of transactions.

qs.q: There are four basic computer sizes, generally classified according to their processing power. Which of these is NOT a computer size designation?
qs.x: A multiprocessor is not a computer size. Note: Lecture 1 actually lists five sizes - supercomputer, mainframe, workstation, microcomputer and microcontroller.

qs.q: What are desktop, notebook, tablet PC, and handheld computers classified as?
qs.x: Desktops, notebooks, tablets and handhelds are all microcomputers.

qs.q: What category does users’ personal computers commonly belong to?
qs.x: Personal computers belong to the microcomputer category.

qs.q: Which computer system is most suitable for use by an average university student?
qs.x: A student needs a microcomputer (PC/laptop), not a mainframe or supercomputer.

qs.q: Which of the following types of computers is the most portable?
qs.x: Of those listed, the laptop is the most portable computer.

qs.q: The Apple iPhone is a cellphone with a microprocessor, display screen, memory and built-in modem. Thus, what is it called?
qs.x: A phone with a processor, screen, memory and modem is a smartphone.

qs.q: According to Lecture 1, what is a computer?
o: A machine that accepts input data and instructions, processes them and produces useful output
An electronic device that can think and make decisions on its own
A machine that only stores information permanently
A device used only for typing documents and printing them
qs.x: A computer accepts data and instructions, processes them, and produces information.

qs.q: What is hardware?
o: The physical or tangible parts of a computer
Raw facts and figures entered into a computer
Computer programs that run on a computer
qs.x: Hardware is the physical parts; software is the programs that run on it.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four basic operations of a computer?
qs.x: The four basic operations are input, processing, storage and output (plus communications).

qs.q: What does the communications function of a computer involve?
qs.x: Communications is the fifth function: sending and receiving data, e.g. through a modem.

qs.q: Primary storage (memory) is best described as:
o: Temporary storage for data waiting to be processed
Backup storage kept in a separate location
Permanent storage for data the computer is not currently using
Storage that keeps data after power is switched off
qs.x: Primary storage is temporary storage for data waiting to be processed; secondary storage is permanent.

qs.q: Which type of memory is volatile, meaning its contents are lost when the computer is switched off?
qs.x: RAM is volatile (like a workbench); ROM is non-volatile.

qs.q: Which statement about secondary storage is TRUE?
o: It is relatively slow and cheaper than main memory, and keeps data when power is off
It loses its contents when power is switched off
It stores only the data the CPU is currently processing
It is faster and more expensive than main memory
qs.x: Secondary (mass) storage is persistent, relatively slow and cheaper than main memory.

qs.q: Which storage medium is commonly used for backup storage?
qs.x: Lecture 1 lists magnetic tape as common for backup storage.

qs.q: What are peripheral devices?
o: External devices connected to the system unit to provide input and output
Files stored on the hard disk
Programs installed on the operating system
The internal circuits of the central processing unit
qs.x: Peripherals are external devices connected to the system unit, e.g. keyboard, printer.

qs.q: Which of the following can act as BOTH an input and an output device?
qs.x: Touch screens, external hard drives and digital camcorders are both input and output.

qs.q: Which part of the CPU coordinates all hardware operations and controls the order in which instructions are carried out?
qs.x: The control unit carries out instructions and coordinates all hardware operations.

qs.q: Which memory works closely with the CPU to hold data and instructions for processing?
qs.x: Main memory works with the CPU to hold data and instructions being processed.

qs.q: Computers are able to perform large numbers of tasks without getting tired. Why does this matter?
o: It removes the mistakes that creep in when tired humans work for long periods
It increases the size of the monitor
It allows the computer to think for itself
It makes the computer cheaper to buy
qs.x: A program can run for days without the fatigue errors humans would make.

qs.q: Telemedicine is an example of computers being used in which area of everyday life?
qs.x: Telemedicine lets doctors treat patients from far away using telecommunications.

qs.q: Online or distance learning, tutoring, simulation and avatars are examples of computer use in:
qs.x: Lecture 1 lists these under Education: more interactive and individualised learning.

qs.q: On what basis are computers generally classified into categories?
o: Speed, processing capability, price and size
Operating system, browser and keyboard layout
qs.x: Classification is by speed, processing capabilities, price and size.

qs.q: Which computer category is used for government census, weather forecasting and designing aircraft?
qs.x: Supercomputers handle quadrillions of calculations for census, weather and scientific work.

qs.q: Which computers are used by banks, airlines and insurance companies for millions of transactions and hundreds of simultaneous users?
qs.x: Mainframes support hundreds of users and critical applications such as records and registration.

qs.q: Expensive, powerful personal computers used for CAD, CAM, designing cars and movie special effects are called:
qs.x: Workstations are powerful PCs for technical, scientific and professional applications.

qs.q: Tiny specialised microprocessors embedded inside microwaves, air-bag sensors and digital cameras are called:
qs.x: Microcontrollers (embedded computers) sit inside appliances and automobiles.

qs.q: Which of the following is a type of microcomputer?
qs.x: Microcomputers include desktops, towers, notebooks, netbooks, tablets, PDAs and e-readers.

qs.q: In a client-server network, what are the PCs and devices that are linked to the server called?
qs.x: The devices that request services from the server are called clients.

qs.q: The word 'server' describes what about a computer?
o: The way the computer is used
The country it was made in
qs.x: A mainframe, workstation or PC can all be servers; the word describes how it is used.

qs.q: Which sequence correctly shows how a computer's parts work together?
o: Input device, CPU and memory, output device, storage device
CPU, storage device, input device, output device
Storage device, output device, CPU, input device
Output device, CPU, input device, storage
qs.x: Data is input, processed by the CPU with memory, output, then stored for later use.

qs.q: A printer, scanner and photocopier combined into one machine shows that:
o: Some devices can be used for several purposes
Output devices are also storage devices
A printer is an input device only
qs.x: Lecture 1 notes that some devices combine several purposes in one unit.

qs.q: Which of these is an example of application software?
qs.x: Application software does user tasks; the others are system software.

qs.q: What does the acronym GUI stand for?
qs.x: GUI = Graphical User Interface: you work with icons, windows and a mouse.

qs.q: What type of user interface allows users to interact with the computer by typing in commands and pressing special keyboard keys?
qs.x: In a command line interface you type commands instead of clicking icons.

qs.q: Which element of a graphical user interface shows programs which are currently running in the computer system?
qs.x: The taskbar shows the programs currently running.

qs.q: In a Graphical User Interface system
o: a window may hold several buttons
a button may hold several windows
several buttons may hold several windows
qs.x: A window can contain many buttons; a button never contains a window.

qs.q: What does a Desktop shortcut refer to?
o: a way to access an application
qs.x: A shortcut is just a link that gives quick access to an application or file.

qs.q: In Windows OS, what is Windows Explorer?
qs.x: Windows Explorer (File Explorer) is the file manager.

qs.q: Which of the following does Microsoft Windows use to organize files?
qs.x: Windows organises files using a file system (tree of drives, folders, files).

qs.q: Which of the following are file management basic operations?
qs.x: Basic file operations: read, write and delete (also create, copy, move, rename).

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a file manipulation task?
qs.x: 'Extend' is not a file task; rename, copy and edit are.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding files?
o: Files are stored in ROM temporarily
A file is a collection of related pieces of information stored together for easy access
Files can be organized using folders
Files can be generated from an application
qs.x: Files are stored on secondary storage, not temporarily in ROM.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the main classifications of a file?
qs.x: Main file classifications: data, program and directory files. 'Density files' does not exist.

qs.q: Tristan just downloaded a new game he wants to play on his computer. What kind of file should he open in order to install and run the game?
qs.x: An executable (.exe) file installs and runs a program.

qs.q: Which of the following can be best used to describe the contents of a file?
qs.x: The file name is what describes the contents; the extension shows the type.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid file property?
qs.x: Type, size and date modified are file properties; 'date printed' is not.

qs.q: Which access right does NOT allow the ordinary user to make changes to a file?
qs.x: Read access lets you open a file but not change it.

qs.q: Which of the following is a valid folder name?
qs.x: Folder names cannot contain \ / : * ? " < > | , so only the underscore name is valid.

qs.q: With regard to C:\ub\253\3\tst.xls, what is C: commonly called?
qs.x: C: is the root folder, at the very top of the file system tree.

qs.q: Which file path best arranges the teachers’ files in schools, with the schools files in a district?
qs.x: Work from the biggest container down: district, then schools, then teachers.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT true?
o: A directory is not the same as a folder
A folder can contain another folder
A file maybe an operating system's file
qs.x: A directory IS the same thing as a folder, so that statement is false.

qs.q: In Windows, which of the following will be the best option to view file sizes and the modified dates of all files in a folder?
qs.x: Details view shows size, type and date modified for every file.

qs.q: Which one of the software works by removing redundant data to reduce file size?
qs.x: File compression removes redundant data to shrink a file (e.g. .zip).

qs.q: Which system utility creates duplicates of the files and programs on a system?
qs.x: A backup utility makes duplicate copies of files and programs.

qs.q: Which of the following is more likely to be a word processor's file?
qs.x: .doc / .docx are Microsoft Word files; .xls is Excel and .txt is plain text.

qs.q: What term is used to refer to information used to identify a document, such as the author or the document purpose?
qs.x: Right-click a file and choose Properties to see name, type, size, author and dates.

qs.q: Which wildcard represents a single character?
qs.x: ? substitutes exactly one character; * substitutes none or many.

qs.q: What is the Windows desktop?
o: The main screen area you see after you turn on the computer and log on to Windows
A program used to browse the Internet
A folder that stores all your documents
The physical table the computer stands on
qs.x: The desktop is Windows' main working surface, like the top of a real desk.

qs.q: When you first start Windows, which icon appears on the desktop?
qs.x: At least one icon always appears at first: the Recycle Bin.

qs.q: How do you open the item that a desktop icon represents?
o: Drag the icon to the taskbar
qs.x: Double-clicking a desktop icon opens the item it represents.

qs.q: How do you identify a shortcut icon?
o: By the arrow on the icon
By its position on the right of the screen
By the dot after its name
qs.x: Shortcuts carry a small arrow on their icon.

qs.q: What happens when you delete a shortcut from the desktop?
o: Only the shortcut is removed; the original item is not deleted
Both the shortcut and the original item are deleted
The original item is moved to the desktop
Nothing happens until you restart the computer
qs.x: Deleting a shortcut removes the link only; deleting an actual item deletes the item.

qs.q: Which sequence creates a shortcut on the desktop?
o: Right-click the item, click Send to, then click Desktop (create shortcut)
Double-click the item, then press Delete
Drag the item into the Recycle Bin
Right-click the desktop, then click Personalize
qs.x: Right-click the item > Send to > Desktop (create shortcut).

qs.q: Where is the notification area found?
o: At the far right of the taskbar, with a clock and a group of icons
On the title bar of the active window
At the top left of every window
qs.x: The notification area sits at the far right of the taskbar and holds the clock and icons.

qs.q: Which steps make Windows arrange desktop icons automatically?
o: Right-click an empty area of the desktop, click View, then click Auto arrange icons
qs.x: Right-click the desktop > View > Auto arrange icons.

qs.q: Which option hides or shows all desktop icons?
o: Right-click the desktop, click View, then click Show desktop icons
Right-click the desktop, then click Personalize
qs.x: View > Show desktop icons toggles the tick that displays or hides icons.

qs.q: How do you select a group of icons on the desktop at once?
o: Click an empty area and drag the mouse so the rectangle surrounds the icons
qs.x: Drag a rectangle around them, then release the mouse; they can then be moved or deleted together.

qs.q: What happens to a file immediately after you delete it in Windows?
o: It goes to the Recycle Bin and can be recovered
It is permanently erased at once
It is copied to a backup drive
qs.x: Deleted items go to the Recycle Bin first, so accidental deletions can be recovered.

qs.q: What happens when you empty the Recycle Bin?
o: Items are permanently deleted and disk space is reclaimed
Items are moved back to the desktop
Items are emailed to you as a backup
qs.x: Emptying the bin deletes the items for good and frees the disk space.

qs.q: Which window control button shrinks a window to the taskbar without closing it?
qs.x: Minimize hides the window to the taskbar; Close ends the program.

qs.q: Which part of a window displays the name of the open file or program?
qs.x: The title bar is at the top and also carries the window control buttons.

qs.q: What is a scroll bar used for?
o: Moving the view up, down or across the contents of a window
qs.x: Scroll bars move the visible area over content too large for the window.

qs.q: What is a file?
o: A resource for storing information that remains available after the program that created it finishes
A temporary area of RAM used by the CPU
A physical part of the system unit
qs.x: A file is durable storage of information, the counterpart of a paper document.

qs.q: What is the maximum length of a file name in Windows?
qs.x: Windows allows file names of up to 255 characters.

qs.q: Which of these characters is NOT allowed in a Windows file name?
qs.x: These are not allowed: \ / : * ? " < > |

qs.q: In the file name lecture2.pptx, what is 'pptx'?
o: The extension, which shows the type of contents
The folder that holds the file
qs.x: A file name is name-dot-extension; the extension gives the type of contents.

qs.q: Which extension belongs to a Microsoft Excel file?
qs.x: .xls/.xlsx = Excel, .doc/.docx = Word, .ppt/.pptx = PowerPoint, .exe = executable.

qs.q: What are file attributes?
o: Settings that grant or deny rights on how a user or the OS can access the file
The names of folders on the C: drive
The speed at which a file opens
The words typed inside a document
qs.x: Attributes such as read, archive, system and hidden control access to a file.

qs.q: Which file attribute tells Windows Backup to back up the file?
qs.x: Archive marks a file for backup; Hidden keeps it out of normal view.

qs.q: Which attribute keeps a file out of view under normal viewing conditions?
qs.x: Hidden files are not displayed unless you choose to show hidden items.

qs.q: Which attribute is tagged to folders to distinguish them from ordinary files?
qs.x: The Directory attribute marks folders and sub-folders.

qs.q: Which attribute is used to prevent unauthorised access to a file?
qs.x: Encryption protects the contents; compression only reduces the size.

qs.q: How do you view the attributes or properties of a file?
o: Right-click the file name and select Properties
Drag the file to the Recycle Bin
qs.x: Right-click > Properties shows name, location, type, size and dates.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT shown in a file's properties?
qs.x: Properties show name, location, type, associated program, size and dates.

qs.q: What does file management mean?
o: Organising and arranging files in a computer
Connecting a computer to the Internet
Increasing the speed of the CPU
qs.x: File management is organising and arranging files, usually through a file manager.

qs.q: Two copies of a file stored in the same folder:
qs.x: Files in one folder must have unique names.

qs.q: Why would you rename homework1.doc to homeworkFinal.doc?
o: To reflect changes made to the contents of the file
To move the file to another folder
qs.x: Renaming is used to keep the name meaningful as the contents change.

qs.q: Which of these is good practice when managing files?
o: Group all related files in one folder and always keep a backup
Keep every file on the desktop
Give files random names so they are hard to guess
qs.x: Lecture 2 tips: meaningful names, revision dates, group related files, sort them, back up.

qs.q: What does backing up files mean?
o: Making copies of files in a separate location so they can be restored
Deleting old files to free space
qs.x: Backups are copies kept elsewhere to protect against disaster or accidental deletion.

qs.q: What is a folder?
o: A location that stores multiple files and other folders
A shortcut to the Recycle Bin
A type of secondary storage device
qs.x: Folders are containers that organise files and can contain other folders.

qs.q: What are folders called when working at the command line?
qs.x: On a command line, folders are referred to as directories.

qs.q: Which sequence creates a new folder on the desktop?
o: Right-click a blank part of the desktop, click New, then click Folder
qs.x: Right-click the desktop > New > Folder; it is called 'New folder' by default.

qs.q: What default name does Windows give a newly created folder?
qs.x: A new folder is named 'New folder' until you rename it.

qs.q: Which steps rename a folder?
o: Right-click the folder, click Rename, type the new name and press ENTER
Double-click the folder and press Delete
Drag the folder to the taskbar
Right-click the desktop and click View
qs.x: Right-click > Rename > type the name > ENTER.

qs.q: The Windows file system is best described as:
o: A tree-like structure with a root folder at the top
A table of file attributes only
A single list of all files in alphabetical order
qs.x: Disk space is partitioned, drives are lettered, and the root folder sits at the top of the tree.

qs.q: What is a pathname?
o: The path taken through a file system to reach a file
The name given to a printer on a network
The list of attributes of a file
The speed at which a file is opened
qs.x: A pathname traces the route through folders to a file.

qs.q: C:\Documents\ICT121\letter1.docx is an example of which type of pathname?
qs.x: It starts from the root (C:), so it is absolute.

qs.q: If you are already in the Documents folder, ICT121\week1.docx is an example of:
qs.x: A relative path starts from your current location rather than the root.

qs.q: What does the * wildcard stand for in a search?
qs.x: * substitutes zero or more characters; ? substitutes exactly one.

qs.q: Which files would the search ????.txt find?
o: Only .txt files whose names are exactly four characters long
Only files with four dots in the name
qs.x: Each ? stands for one character, so the name must be exactly four characters.

qs.q: Which file name does moswetsi?b.abc match?
qs.x: ? matches exactly one character, so only one character may sit before the b.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT an option you can search a file by in Windows?
qs.x: You can search by name, date, type and size.

qs.q: Which of the following in considered to be the world’s biggest WAN?
qs.x: The Internet is the world's biggest wide area network.

qs.q: Which network is designed to share information and is accessible only to the organization’s members?
qs.x: An intranet uses Internet technology but is for an organisation's members only.

qs.q: What does the acronym WWW stand for?
qs.x: WWW = World Wide Web.

qs.q: Which one of the following is not an example of a Web browser?
qs.x: Chrome, Firefox and Internet Explorer are browsers; Windows Explorer is a file manager.

qs.q: Which of the following is an example of a search engine?
qs.x: Google is a search engine; Opera and Internet Explorer are browsers.

qs.q: Which of these can be used to locate information on the web by asking questions or using keywords?
qs.x: Search engines find information on the web from keywords or questions.

qs.q: Which of the following is a connection used to navigate between different documents in a website?
qs.x: A hyperlink is the link you click to move between documents/pages.

qs.q: Which extension will you use in webpage development?
qs.x: Web pages are written in HTML, so the extension is .html

qs.q: In the URL http://www.gec.com/first.htm, what does http refer to?
qs.x: In a URL, http is the protocol (the first part before ://).

qs.q: What does the term FTP stand for?
qs.x: FTP = File Transfer Protocol, used to move files between hosts.

qs.q: Suppose ICT121 club wants to register a domain name using their name. Which of the following domain names will not be valid?
qs.x: Domain names cannot start with a symbol or contain invalid characters/format.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of an internal storage device?
qs.x: A web server shares an information resource with multiple users.

qs.q: Which one of the following scenarios most likely suggests that a computer is online?
o: When it is running a web browser
When it has loaded the Operating System
When it is connected to a USB flash disk
When it is running as a word processor
qs.x: A computer running a web browser (connected to the Internet) is online.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT considered a part of cyberspace?
qs.x: Cyberspace covers online spaces such as blogs, the Internet and conference calls; a printer is hardware.

qs.q: Where do you save a website that you like to visit frequently?
qs.x: Favourites (bookmarks) save sites you visit often.

qs.q: What term is used to describe the buying of goods on the Internet?
qs.x: Buying goods over the Internet is online shopping (e-shopping).

qs.q: What is an uninvited email solicitation to buy something an example of?
qs.x: Unsolicited bulk advertising email is spam.

qs.q: What is the feature that automatically routes advertisements and other junk mail to the Deleted folder maintained by your e-mail client called?
qs.x: A spam filter automatically moves junk mail to the deleted/junk folder.

qs.q: Which of the following is TRUE about email use?
o: the size of the mail box is limited, thus not everybody can send you an email
the size of the mail box is huge, thus everybody can send you an email
the size of the mail box is limited, thus everybody can send you an email
the size of the mail box is not limited, thus everybody can send you an email
qs.x: Mailbox size is limited, so a full mailbox can stop mail reaching you.

qs.q: Which definition best describes the Internet?
o: A worldwide computer network that connects hundreds of thousands of smaller networks
A single computer that stores all the web pages in the world
A program used to view web pages
A company that sells web addresses
qs.x: The Internet is a network of networks linking educational, commercial, non-profit and military entities.

qs.q: Which protocol suite do the networks of the Internet use to link devices worldwide?
qs.x: The Internet uses the standard Internet Protocol suite, TCP/IP.

qs.q: Who owns the Internet?
o: No one person or organisation owns or controls it in its entirety
qs.x: Nobody owns the Internet; it is a concept relying on physical infrastructure that links networks.

qs.q: Which of these is another name for the Internet?
qs.x: Also called the Net, the Information Superhighway and Cyberspace.

qs.q: How does an extranet differ from an intranet?
o: An extranet also allows use by selected outside entities such as suppliers
An extranet does not use Internet standards
An extranet is only for a single user
An extranet is another name for the World Wide Web
qs.x: Intranet = internal use only; extranet = internal plus selected outsiders.

qs.q: Which of the following is an Internet service or use listed in Lecture 3?
qs.x: Services include email, research, news, entertainment, downloading, e-shopping, e-business and social networking.

qs.q: Which statement about the World Wide Web is TRUE?
o: The web is an information-sharing model built on top of the Internet, so www is not the same as the Internet
The web is a cable that carries Internet traffic
The web and the Internet are exactly the same thing
The web is a type of web browser
qs.x: The web is a way of accessing information over the Internet; www is not equal to the Internet.

qs.q: What is hypertext?
o: Text with references (hyperlinks) to other text that the reader can immediately access
Text written only in capital letters
Text that has been printed in bold
qs.x: Hypertext carries hyperlinks that take the reader straight to other documents.

qs.q: What does HTML stand for?
qs.x: HTML is the authoring language used to create documents on the World Wide Web.

qs.q: What is a web browser?
o: A software application for retrieving, presenting and traversing information resources on the web
A language used to write web pages
A cable that connects to the Internet
qs.x: A browser is the client software that requests and displays web resources.

qs.q: In the client-server model of the web, what is the browser?
o: The client that contacts the web server and requests information
The domain name of the website
The server that stores the pages
The protocol used to transfer pages
qs.x: The browser is the client; the web server sends the information back.

qs.q: Microbrowsers are:
o: Browsers designed for web access through mobile devices
Browsers that only open small files
qs.x: Mobile browsers are stripped-down browsers optimised for small screens and less memory.

qs.q: What is a website?
o: A collection of one or more web pages grouped under the same domain name
The software used to view web pages
qs.x: A web page is one document; a website is a collection of pages under one domain name.

qs.q: What is a domain name?
o: The website's name, the address where Internet users access your website
The protocol used to open a page
The title shown at the top of a web page
The name of the browser you are using
qs.x: For example www.ActNowDomains.com is that website's domain name.

qs.q: A URL consists of which three parts?
o: Network protocol, host name or address, and file or resource location
qs.x: The form is protocol://host/location.

qs.q: Which of these is a typical URL protocol?
qs.x: Typical protocols include http://, ftp:// and mailto://

qs.q: Which describes a static web page?
o: It is delivered exactly as stored and displays the same information for all users at all times
It changes with time, user and context
It is used for stock prices and weather updates
It requires server-side scripting such as PHP
qs.x: Static pages are plain .html files, easy to create, the same for everyone.

qs.q: Where are dynamic web pages most useful?
o: Where information changes frequently, such as stock prices and weather
Where only printed output is needed
Where a student's personal profile never changes
qs.x: Dynamic pages are prepared fresh for each viewing, based on time, user or context.

qs.q: JavaScript is an example of which type of scripting?
qs.x: JavaScript runs on the client for presentation; ASP and PHP run on the server.

qs.q: PHP and ASP are examples of:
qs.x: Server-side scripts generate the page content before it reaches the browser.

qs.q: What is HTTP used for?
o: Viewing web pages; it is the foundation of data communication for the web
Sending files between two hosts only
qs.x: HTTP is the protocol used for viewing web pages.

qs.q: How does HTTPS differ from HTTP?
o: It encrypts the data being retrieved, instead of sending everything in clear text
It is faster but less reliable
It transfers files instead of pages
qs.x: In standard HTTP all information is sent in clear text; HTTPS adds encryption.

qs.q: What is SSL?
o: A standard security protocol for establishing an encrypted link between a server and a client
A language for writing web pages
qs.x: SSL secures sensitive data such as card numbers and login credentials in transit.

qs.q: Which security protocol is the successor to SSL?
qs.x: TLS is the latest industry-standard cryptographic protocol, the successor to SSL.

qs.q: AES is best described as:
o: An encryption algorithm for securing sensitive data over the Internet
A browser plug-in for playing video
qs.x: Advanced Encryption Standard is an encryption algorithm.

qs.q: What is a firewall?
o: A system designed to prevent unauthorised access to or from a private network
A program that removes viruses from email
A device that speeds up the Internet connection
A backup copy of a website
qs.x: All messages entering or leaving pass through it and those failing the security criteria are blocked.

qs.q: How are search engine results normally presented?
o: As a list of results, on search engine results pages
As an email to the user
As a single web page with one answer
qs.x: Results are listed on search engine results pages.

qs.q: Who sent the first email, and when?
o: Steve Jobs, in 1976, to Apple staff
Tim Berners-Lee, in 1989, to a colleague
Bill Gates, in 1985, to Microsoft staff
qs.x: The first email was sent in 1971 by Ray Tomlinson to himself.

qs.q: Which email field lists everyone the message is being sent to directly?
qs.x: TO holds the main recipients; CC copies others; BCC copies them invisibly.

qs.q: What is special about recipients placed in the BCC field?
o: They cannot see other recipients and are not visible to the intended recipients
They receive the message before everybody else
They are the only ones who can reply
qs.x: Blind carbon copy hides those addresses from everyone, and hides other recipients from them.

qs.q: Recipients placed in the CC field:
o: Can see the original recipients and are visible to them
Are hidden from all other recipients
qs.x: Carbon copy recipients are visible, unlike BCC.

qs.q: What does the SUBJECT field of an email hold?
o: The message title that is displayed to the recipient
The date the message was sent
qs.x: SUBJECT is the message title display.

qs.q: Which of the following is an email service provider?
qs.x: Lecture 3 lists Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail, Fastmail, Mail.com and others.
